explain.say: Most big caves form in limestone, a rock made of calcium carbonate. Rainwater picks up carbon dioxide from the air and soil, making it a very weak acid, called carbonic acid.

faq.q: Why do caves form in limestone?
faq.a: Limestone is made of calcium carbonate, which dissolves in slightly acidic water. Most other rocks, like granite, do not dissolve this way, so big caves are rare in them.
asks: Why don't caves form in granite?

faq.a: As rain falls through the air and soaks through soil, it dissolves carbon dioxide gas. This makes a very weak acid called carbonic acid, much weaker than lemon juice.

faq.q: How long does a cave take to form?
faq.a: Usually hundreds of thousands of years or more. The water dissolves only a tiny amount of rock each year, but it keeps working for a very long time.
Karst is a landscape on limestone shaped by dissolving rock. It has caves, sinkholes, disappearing streams and underground rivers.

faq.q: What is the longest cave in the world?
faq.a: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky, USA, with over 680 kilometres of mapped passages, all dissolved in limestone.

facts: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky is the longest known cave system, with more than 680 kilometres mapped.
Limestone is mostly calcium carbonate, which dissolves in weak carbonic acid.
